subject: Re: Data samples + guidelines
text:
Hey James,
Excited to move forward!

We’d absolutely love that. We’ve put together a short overview of the
mission, along with a shareable file you can download that includes videos
to tag.

The task:
Evaluate the clip across the following quality dimensions. For each,
provide:
  - description: one concise sentence describing your observation
  - score: an integer from 1 to 5 per the scale defined below

Score meanings per dimension (5 is always the desirable outcome for dataset
quality):

  video_quality         — 1: severe artifacts / unviewable; 5: crisp,
full-resolution, no encoding issues.
  motion_blur           — 1: pervasive blur obscuring the action; 5: sharp
frames throughout.
  camera_stability      — 1: constant unwanted shake or pan; 5: completely
static and steady.
  robot_movement        — 1: extremely jerky, trembling, or erratic; 5:
smooth and confident throughout.
  task_completion       — 1: robot clearly fails or stops mid-task; 5: task
is completed successfully.
  occlusion             — 1: gripper or key object hidden for most of the
critical action; 5: fully visible at all times.
  object_visibility     — 1: task objects indistinguishable or out of
frame; 5: clearly identifiable throughout.
  lighting              — 1: severely over/underexposed or deep shadows
hiding the action; 5: even, well-lit scene.
  color_fidelity        — 1: heavy color cast, IR artifact, or washed-out
tones; 5: natural, accurate colors.
  background_complexity — 1: extremely cluttered or dynamic background
dominating the scene; 5: clean, minimal, static background.
  human_presence        — 1: significant human body parts dominating the
frame; 5: no human presence visible.
  temporal_consistency  — 1: multiple frame jumps, cuts, or looping
artifacts; 5: smooth continuous playback.
  depth_of_focus        — 1: gripper and object interaction area are
blurred; 5: action area is in sharp focus.

This should be done to the clips I am attaching to this mail
 test_sample_cli

subject: RE: L-1A for: Encord/ Kamil Mouthon - Still need Questionnaire and Checklist - Follow up
text:
Hi Kamil,

Thank you kindly for following up!  I am working on your L-1A paperwork and I'm hoping you will be able to provide me with a bit more information and evidence.  When you have a moment, could you please email me the following:

  1.  Copy of your initial offer letter and any subsequent offer letters or promotional evidence you've received while at Encord.
  2.  Job description of your previous positions at Encord.
  3.  Do you know what your annual salary will be once you enter the US in L-1A status?
  4.  Will you work from the San Francisco, CA office (2261 Market Street)?
  5.  You are currently managing a staff of 5 Commercial Associates. Can you please provide evidence of these employees' employment with Encord?  If possible, please send me their CV and a copy of their job descriptions (you can send just 1 if they all have the same job duties), as well as evidence of their employment at Encord (such as pay stubs).
  6.  I also see the Org Chart of your proposed US position, is this also your current Org Chart for your role in the UK?  Meaning they are the same?

Also, since you are the expert, I'm hoping you can assist with breaking down your specific specialized knowledge.  The USCIS regulations define "Specialized Knowledge" as:

  *   "Special"  knowledge possessed by an individual of the petitioning organization's product, service, research, equipment, techniques, management, or other interests and its application in international markets-NOT special information about the field in general; or
  *   An Advanced level of knowledge or expertise in the organization's processes and procedures."  Important:  it is NOT an advanced knowledge of the field in general, but rather an advanced knowledge of the organization's proprietary or unique processes, procedures, protocols; or advanced knowledge of the company's proprietary information.
  *   The term special can also mean surpassing the usual; distinct among the knowledge held by others at the company;

subject: Encord <> Bosch: Exploratory Discussion – Teleoperation Data Collection for Robotics Foundation Models
text:
Hi Nick,

thank you for your response.

We would be happy to set up an exploratory discussion Thursday at
4:15 PM CEST, which should be 3:15 PM in London.

Please let me know if this time works for you. If not, we can also look for another slot.

The discussion can take place
without an NDA, so we should keep it non-confidential at this stage.

Here are in advance initial keywords and a short wish list to give you a better idea of what we would like to discuss: 

• 

Teleop / custom collection of teleoperated robot data

• 

Synchronized timestamps across all relevant data streams

• 

QA filtering, e.g. removal of failed, blurry or low-quality episodes

• 

LeRobot-compatible annotation format

• 

Embodiment-specific data, including robot state and action data, not video-only, ego-only or general datasets

• 

Relevant scale, roughly in the range of 100 hours per use case

• 

Retargeting / curation capabilities as a nice-to-have

• 

Platform and annotation services as additional nice-to-haves

 The broader context is that Bosch is exploring how to make robotic systems in manufacturing more adaptable and generalizable for production
 use cases that are not yet feasible to automate with conventional approaches. A key requirement for this is access to high-quality, meaningful teleoperated robot data, collected with sufficient process understanding and operator expertise.

From our side, we would provide input on a selected use case, including the physical application scenario and relevant process steps.
 From a partner, we would be interested in understanding capabilities around the collection of synchronized, high-quality annotated teleoperation episodes for a specified robot embodiment and task setup.

There is also an optional interest in discussing additional egocentric human-operator data collection, for example using equipment provided
 by Bosch, but we can go into this in more detail during the call.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen / Best regards

Hans-Peter Grabsc

subject: Re: Bytedance <> Encord - training data
text:
Hi team,

We have reviewed the samples and prepared the feedback as follows:
Teleoperations Data
In my opinion, these samples are incomplete.
• No wrist cameras, and visible occlusions on all available cameras; no multi-view footage, missing depth maps.
• Annotations include clips and corresponding instructions.
• Zero proprioceptive robot data: no joint angles, end-effector poses, gripper opening/closing values, etc.
Egocentric Data
• Data contents: three side views, third-person view, plus depth for the main egocentric camera. Camera quality is good with no motion blur. However, only partial samples are provided with estimated MANO hand poses.
• Diversity: The dataset covers a wide range of scenarios with long-horizon household tasks, which meets our requirements well. 
• We place high priority on data diversity and long-sequence tasks. Could you share how much OTS data you have of this type, along with its data distribution? Could you also provide a price quotation for reference?
Please feel free to contact me if you have any questions.

Best,
Meng
